name: Strata
description: A design system derived from IBM's Carbon Design System (Apache-2.0). Every token records the Carbon value it came from and the reason for any divergence. Not affiliated with or endorsed by IBM. Unbranded scaffold build: the moderate-fidelity render target. Real spacing, type, states and hierarchy with no brand commitment.

org.strata.carbon.why: Carbon's 50% active wash on light themes drops the underlying label to roughly 2.4:1 mid-press. 40% keeps the state legible for the whole duration of the interaction.

background-brand.$description: Brand fill: batch action bars, selected dates

org.strata.carbon.why: Deloitte Green 349 #046A38. Grade 70 reproduces it to within delta-RGB 5 in the light theme. NOT held constant across themes, which is where Carbon does hold it constant: a grade-70 fill on a grade-100 page measures 2.45:1 and barely reads as a surface at all. Dark drops to grade 60 for 3.48:1.

layer-accent-01.$description: Tertiary surface: table headers, zebra rows

org.strata.carbon.value: $field-01 — Gray 10 / Gray 90. 'A field is considered a layer on top of the background it is placed on' — /elements/color/usage/

org.strata.carbon.why: Lightened to the whisper hairline of the 20 Aug 2026 visual language (composites to ~#ececed on white). Separation is carried by the hairline plus the resting shadow, not tone.

border-subtle-01.$description: Standard hairline on controls and dividers

org.strata.carbon.why: One step lighter than Carbon's: grade 20/80 (the old subtle-00 values). Part of the same E-04 re-cut.

Carbon uses Gray 50 for border-strong on every light layer. Against layer-01 (#f4f4f4) that measures 3.02:1 — it passes 1.4.11, but by 0.02. Strata uses neutral-60, which measures 4.62:1 on layer-01 and 4.99:1 on the page background, so the guarantee survives a hue swap or a rounding change.
Moved to grade 70 rather than 60 so it sits with the primary action and opens a clear gap to $support-success at grade 60. 7.1:1 on the page background.

org.strata.carbon.value: No Carbon counterpart — Carbon's tertiary uses a full-strength $button-tertiary border
org.strata.carbon.why: The 20 Aug 2026 language draws tertiary as a white surface with a tinted hairline; grade 30 light / 70 dark keeps it recognisably interactive without competing with primary.

Carbon's light-theme body text is Gray 100 at 17.4:1 on white. That is far past AAA and is a large part of why Carbon reads hard-edged. neutral-90 gives 14.2:1 — still comfortably AAA, measurably softer. Note this is a deliberate reduction in contrast and is the one divergence to revisit if the product targets low-vision users or bright-sunlight field use.

org.strata.carbon.value: $text-placeholder — rgba(22,22,22,0.4) in shipped @carbon/styles; Gray 40 #a8a8a8 in the /elements/color/tokens/ table. The two official sources disagree.
org.strata.carbon.why: Both Carbon values fail 4.5:1 against their own field background (#f4f4f4): the composited rgba value measures 2.53:1, Gray 40 measures 2.16:1. Placeholder is text and WCAG 1.4.3 applies. neutral-60 gives 4.62:1 on field-01 in light; dark uses grade 40, because grade 50 measures only 3.48:1 against field-02 (a field nested on layer-01) — the composited contrast audit caught that, the eye would not have. Carbon's own rule that placeholder must never replace a persistent label is kept and enforced in the component CSS.

text-on-color.$description: Text on a filled interactive surface

org.strata.carbon.why: 25% of Carbon's Gray 100 lands near 1.9:1. Disabled text is exempt from contrast minimums, but 'exempt' is not 'illegible'. 30% reads as clearly-off without becoming invisible.
Red 60 on a Gray 10 field measures ~4.3:1 in Carbon. Grade 70 clears 4.5:1 against every light surface in the system.

Green, matching the interactive colour — a system with two different 'this is clickable' hues teaches nothing. Grade 70 so a link still clears 4.5:1 on layer-01 and inside a filled table row, not only on white.
Follows link-primary.

The one deliberately off-brand token in the system. Deloitte's palette has no purple, and visited-link needs a hue that carries no other meaning here — green is interactive, blue is informational, teal and orange are categorical, red and amber are status. Every Deloitte hue is spoken for. Substituting one would make 'visited' collide with a live signal, which is worse than an off-brand link. Drop visited styling entirely if that trade is unacceptable.
Matched to text-disabled for the same reason.
Brand green.

Value unchanged, but the RELATIONSHIP changed and this is the one token to argue about. With a green brand, success and the primary action are now one grade apart in the same hue (green.60 vs green.70). They are kept apart by form, not by colour: support-success only ever renders as a toggle track, a status icon or a 3px banner rule, never as a filled action-shaped surface, and every status carries an icon under the never-colour-alone rule. The alternative — moving success to teal — breaks the strongest colour convention in UI (green = good) to solve a collision the form language already resolves, and would push info off Deloitte Blue. If user testing says otherwise it is one line: change this to teal.60 / teal.30 and move the tag palette with it.

Two problems fixed at once. (1) Carbon holds Yellow 30 constant across light and dark, breaking the contract that every semantic token re-resolves per theme. (2) Yellow 30 measures ~1.6:1 on white, so a Carbon warning icon fails 1.4.11 against its own notification background — the status that most needs to be noticed is the one that disappears. Strata resolves per theme and drops to grade 60 in light, which measures 4.6:1 on the warning surface. It reads as ochre rather than school-bus yellow; that is the cost of making it visible.

Deloitte Blue 7690 #0076A8, which grade 60 reproduces to within delta-RGB 3. Note this REVERSES a pre-brand divergence: Strata previously moved info to teal because Carbon's blue info collided with Carbon's blue primary action. With a green primary that objection disappears and blue is free, so info returns to Carbon's value. The divergence was contingent on the brand, not on Carbon being wrong — which is the argument for semantic tokens in one example.

Status backgrounds are needed by banners, table cells, form sections and inline validation, not just the Notification component, and Carbon's component-token confinement rule ('should never be used for anything other than their own component') would otherwise force a duplicate.

org.strata.carbon.why: Deloitte Green 349. Grade 70, not 60: the brand's dark green is a 7.1:1 colour, and it leaves grades 80 and 90 free for hover and active. A grade-60 green would have run out of room. The dark theme uses grade 60 instead: at grade 70 the button barely separates from the page (2.45:1), and the near-black $focus-inset ring inside it fell to 2.46:1 — the composited audit caught that, and it is a failure mode a blue primary never had because Carbon's Blue 60 is a lighter colour than Deloitte's dark green.

Dark theme drops a grade. Carbon's dark secondary button is Gray 60 with $text-on-color (white) on it, which measures about 3.5:1 — under 4.5:1 for a button label. Grade 70 gives 7.1:1 and leaves room for the hover to lighten without crossing the threshold.
Follows the base grade. Carbon's dark hover lightens toward Gray 50, where a white label falls to roughly 3.0:1 — the hover state is where the label becomes least readable, which is backwards.

org.strata.carbon.value: $button-danger-hover — #b81921 hardcoded (note: @carbon/colors red60Hover is #b81922 — the two official values differ by one digit)

org.strata.carbon.why: Gray 30 against a white page is a loud disabled state. Grade 20 recedes; the disabled label still reads at ~3.4:1 against it.
Tinted with the neutral hue instead of pure black, and lightened in light themes. Pure black scrims are the other half of why Carbon reads industrial.
Brand green.

A white handle on Carbon's dark-theme $support-success (Green 40) measures about 2.2:1 — the handle, which is the only thing communicating the toggle's position, is the least visible part of it in dark mode. Strata inverts the handle with the theme: 5.0:1 and 4.7:1 in light, 6.6:1 and 4.7:1 in dark, on the on and off tracks respectively.
The caps micro-label of the T1 ramp: weight 500 and wider tracking because it renders uppercase (the class sets text-transform). One label style, not two — label-md retired with the ramp.
T1's small running text: 12px with a taller line and tighter tracking than a label, because it sets sentences, not tags.

THE body size. 13.5px is the T1 working-density body — denser than the previous 16px default (that divergence is hereby reversed), calmer than Carbon's 14 at these weights. Off-scale knowingly; the ramp is hand-tuned, not formula-derived.
Body-size heading: inline heads, card titles, table headers. Same size as body-md — weight alone carries the emphasis, which is the T1 rule.
The section head. One size above body, weight-led, a whisper of negative tracking.

The one display moment: page titles and stat figures. 600 not 300/400 — T1 was chosen over Carbon's light-display treatment by eye, on identical pages. Negative tracking per the large-text rule the old heading-lg established.
Every identifier renders mono — the house signature. Drops from code-02 metrics to code-01 with the ramp.

spacing.value: spacing-01..13 = 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 160px. Carbon's own wording: the scale uses 'multiples of two, four, and eight'. Note the 8px mini unit is a 2x GRID concept, not the basis of the spacing scale — 2, 4 and 12 are not multiples of 8. The two are complementary, not the same rule.
spacing.why: Adopted wholesale, all 13 values. This is the single strongest part of Carbon: a 13-step scale on multiples of 2/4/8 covers everything from icon insets to page gutters without anyone reaching for an arbitrary number.

size.value: Carbon control heights: xs 24, sm 32, md 40, lg 48, xl 64, 2xl 80. Default for product UI is large-productive (48) for buttons, medium (40) for fields.
size.why: The scale is kept 1:1 so anything ported from Carbon maps without arithmetic. What changes is the DEFAULT: Strata defaults every interactive control to lg (48px), fields included. Carbon's own accessibility guidance requires 'all touch targets for interactive icons need to be 44px or larger' (/elements/icons/usage/) yet its default field is 40px -- an internal inconsistency. Defaulting to 48 clears the 44px floor for every control, not just icons. 32px remains available for data-dense surfaces. xs (24) is carried because Carbon carries it and the resolution map cites it for table row height -- but it is a ROW height only. It is below the 44px touch floor and must never size an interactive control.

radius.value: Carbon has no radius scale, no radius token in @carbon/layout or @carbon/themes, and no published square-corner rule or rationale anywhere on the site. Four component pages do publish a radius — Tag 16px, Content switcher 4px, Code snippet 2px, Popover 2px — while 23 component SCSS files set border-radius in shipped code (button, checkbox, toggle, tile, tooltip, slider, list-box...).
radius.why: Worth being precise, because 'Carbon is square-cornered' is folklore. It is not a documented rule. What Carbon actually has is radius applied ad hoc in 23 files with only four values ever documented — which is the definition of a scale that should exist and doesn't. Strata makes it explicit and moves the control default from 0 to 6px. Because it is a token, reverting the whole system to square is a one-line change.

elevation.value: One shadow mixin: `box-shadow: 0 2px 6px $shadow` where $shadow is black @30% (light themes) / @80% (dark). Plus a hardcoded 0 2px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.2) on Popover. Carbon states: 'Tiles reside on the same plane as the page background layer and do not have elevation... Do not add a drop shadow to tiles.'
elevation.why: Strata keeps the layering model as the primary depth mechanism for in-flow surfaces -- that part of Carbon is excellent and is why Carbon reads calm. But a single 30%-black shadow is blunt: it is too heavy for a dropdown and too weak for a modal, which is exactly why Carbon had to hardcode a different one on Popover. Strata publishes three levels, all two-layer (tight contact shadow + diffuse ambient) and all tinted with the neutral hue rather than pure black, which is the single biggest contributor to a 'softer' surface read.

breakpoint.value: Carbon breakpoints: sm 320, md 672, lg 1056, xlg 1312, max 1584.

sans.why: Re-adopted 20 Aug 2026 (was 'changed' to Inter-first; see the ledger). OFL-1.1 obligations recorded above and in LICENCE-AND-ATTRIBUTION.md §2.

mono.value: 'IBM Plex Mono', 'Menlo', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Courier, monospace
mono.why: Same reasoning and same obligations as the sans face.

button.summary: Primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost and danger, in three sizes.
spec: Carbon: seven sizes across two variants — button xs 24, sm 32, md 40, large-productive 48, large-expressive 48; full-bleed button xl 64, 2xl 80

Same scale, default moved to 48 to clear the 44px touch floor. The two 48s and the full-bleed-only 64/80 are collapsed: a size scale with two entries at the same height is a naming artefact, not a size.

Carbon: 16px left / 64px right on a button with NO icon. Buttons with icons, icon-only buttons and all ghost buttons are already 16/16. Carbon's stated basis: 'When we say "fixed," there is a fixed padding of 16px to the left and a 64px padding to the right of the button label. The button label determines the button's width.' Paired with the Do caption 'Do left-align the label in a button, even if the button is wide.'

Narrower than it first looks — Carbon is already symmetric in four of five cases, so this changes one. Carbon does publish a rationale for the 16 (nothing within 16px of a border; >=16px between label and icon so adjacent icon buttons stay separable) but none for the 64. The result is a button whose visual centre of mass sits left of its geometric centre, which is why a separate left-align rule is needed to keep it consistent. Strata centres the label instead.
Carbon: not published on the style page, and _button.scss sets no border-radius
Carbon: 16x16 icon (20x20 expressive); 32px label-to-icon gap on filled buttons, 8px on ghost
One gap value. The 32px filled-button gap is a consequence of the 64px right pad, not an independent decision.
2px focus ring, inset, + 1px focus-inset ring on filled variants

Carbon: the style page publishes only colours ($focus border, $focus-inset inset) plus 'box-shadow: inset | 1px'. Shipped code is a 1px border that turns $focus, with box-shadow inset 1px $focus AND inset 2px in the button's own background colour — so the visible double ring is 1px+2px, not 2px+1px.

Strata uses the generic 2px/-2px geometry from Carbon's own focus-outline mixin for every control including buttons, rather than button's bespoke 1px border-plus-two-shadows construction. Same two-tone mechanism, one implementation.
Primary right in dialogs and wizards; primary left on full pages

text-input.summary: Text input, textarea and the shared field chrome.
spec: Default moved to lg, as with buttons.
Carbon: border-bottom 1px $border-strong only; no side or top border

Carbon's underline-only field is the strongest single signal of its visual identity, and the hardest to defend. A field with no left, right or top edge does not read as a container, its click target is ambiguous, and adjacent fields in a row visually merge. Carbon then has to switch to a full 2px border on focus and on error — so the boxed form already exists in the system, it is just withheld from the resting state. A full 1px border makes the resting, focus and error states the same shape.
2px support-error border, icon, message replaces helper text
Carbon: border 2px $support-error, message $text-error at $label-01, replaces helper
amber icon; message in text-primary; border unchanged

Carbon: identical — warning icon $support-warning, warning message $text-primary at $label-01, and no border row at all for the warning state. Carbon publishes no rationale for the asymmetry with error.
24px between fields; 48px before the button row

Carbon (forms pattern page, not the text-input style page): 'we recommend a 32px spacer between input fields' on dedicated pages, 'designers can revert to 24px or even 16px' in contained forms, and 'a 48px spacer between the last input and the button or button group'. The Form style page gives a partly different set again.
One value instead of three. 32px at a 14px body was proportionate; at a 16px body with taller controls it over-separates.
Carbon: 16x16px, 1px border. Radius is not published on the style page, but _checkbox.scss ships border-radius: 2px — the 2px is Carbon's own value, just undocumented.

Carbon: checkbox items 4px apart, radio items 8px apart
Carbon states both values on its two style pages. Unified at 8px.
body-md, 8px to the left of the label

Wrapped label text top-aligns to the control

Carbon: 'The default view of a radio button is having no radio button preselected.'
Carbon: 18px (published as '18/1.25' — the rem value is wrong, 18px is 1.125rem) / 10px
Value adopted; the docs typo noted.

Carbon: 'Ideal for settings or preferences that can be immediately applied.' and 'Avoid using toggles for settings that aren't binary in nature or don't provide instant application; instead use a different UI component, like a checkbox, in combination with a button.'

spec: Carbon: matches; menu item height matches field height
Carbon: 48px ($spacing-09) on both the dropdown and select structure tables — though _dropdown.scss actually ships 42px, so Carbon's own code disagrees with its published value
40px clears a 16px chevron with 16px of inset at 48px tall, and it is one value rather than two.

A scroll threshold IS published: 'We recommend starting a scroll at the sixth option in the menu list' while 'showing 50% of the last option's container height to indicate there is more to see'. Shipped as max-block-size 220px (40px item x 5.5).
Carbon's rule restated at Strata's row height — 320px is six 48px rows, the same intent as Carbon's 220px at 40px rows. Strata publishes the px value as well as the rule, so it can be a token.
Carbon (select usage page, not dropdown): 'It is best practice not to use a select if there are fewer than three options for selection. In this case, use a radio button group instead.'

start / in range / end each explicitly specified

A real gap in Carbon — the React implementation supports it, the design system never specified it.
xs 320 / sm 480 / md 640 / lg 880px, capped at calc(100vw - 32px)

Carbon: 'Modal widths are defined as percentages of the browser but will still align to columns on the 2x grid' — xs 24%, sm 36%, md 48%, lg 72% at 1584, with column spans (4/6/8/12 of 16) but no px values published anywhere

Percentage-of-viewport widths mean a dialog's measure changes with the browser, so body copy runs to 90+ characters on a wide monitor. Fixed max-widths with a viewport cap hold the measure constant, which is what dialog copy needs.
Carbon: buttons span 50% of the modal each and bleed to its edges; three buttons are 25% each
Full-bleed 50% buttons make Cancel exactly as visually heavy as the primary action, which is the opposite of what a confirmation dialog should do.

Carbon: $overlay, black @60%, identical in all four themes
Body scrolls; header and footer stay fixed. No horizontal scroll.
First field, or the primary button if there is no field. Esc closes.
Carbon: 40px for both line and contained
Carbon: border-bottom 2px $border-interactive; label switches from $body-compact-01 to $heading-compact-01 (400 -> 600)
Adopted including the weight change — it is what makes the selected tab survive greyscale, satisfying 'don't rely on colour alone'.
1px border-subtle-01 underline across the whole tab list
Carbon: border-bottom 2px $border-subtle ($tab-underline-color) — the same width as the selected state, only the colour changes

1px at rest, 2px selected. Carbon's equal-width treatment means the resting underline carries as much visual weight as the selection indicator, so the selected tab has to rely on colour plus weight to separate itself. Halving the rest state lets the 2px selected rule read as an indicator rather than a recolour.

Carbon: 16px at every size — one of only four radii Carbon publishes on a component page (Tag 16px, Content switcher 4px, Code snippet 2px, Popover 2px), against 22 component SCSS files that set one
